learn.peon-1.title: The Pawn
learn.peon-1.desc: The pawn moves forward and captures diagonally. Complete the 8 exercises in order.
learn.peon-1.success: Pawn chapter complete! It moves straight ahead, captures diagonally, and promotes when it reaches the last rank.
learn.peon-1.s0.title: Advance
learn.peon-1.s0.instruction: Move the pawn forward to the star.
learn.peon-1.s0.hint: The pawn moves one square. Take it from d2 to d3.
learn.peon-1.s1.title: Double step
learn.peon-1.s1.instruction: From its starting square the pawn can advance two squares.
learn.peon-1.s1.hint: Only on its first move can the pawn advance two squares: from d2 to d4.
learn.peon-1.s2.title: Step by step
learn.peon-1.s2.instruction: Advance the pawn square by square to the stars.
learn.peon-1.s2.hint: After the first step, the pawn only advances one square at a time.
learn.peon-1.s3.title: Capture
learn.peon-1.s3.instruction: The pawn captures diagonally. Capture the black piece!
learn.peon-1.s3.hint: The pawn captures diagonally forward: from d2 to e3.
learn.peon-1.s4.title: Capture and advance
learn.peon-1.s4.instruction: Capture diagonally and then keep advancing.
learn.peon-1.s4.hint: First capture on e3 and then go straight to e4.
learn.peon-1.s5.title: Two captures
learn.peon-1.s5.hint: Capture on e3 and from there capture again diagonally toward f4.
learn.peon-1.s6.title: Promote
learn.peon-1.s6.instruction: Take the pawn to the last rank to promote.
learn.peon-1.s6.hint: Advance from d7 to d8: the pawn becomes a piece (usually a queen!).
learn.peon-1.s7.title: Promote by advancing
learn.peon-1.s7.instruction: Advance the pawn to the last rank and promote.
learn.peon-1.s7.hint: Advance to d7 and then to d8 to promote.
learn.caballo-1.title: The Knight
learn.caballo-1.desc: The knight moves in an "L" shape and is the only piece that jumps over others. Complete the 6 exercises in order.
learn.caballo-1.success: Knight chapter complete! It jumps in an "L" and can leap over any piece.
learn.caballo-1.s0.title: L-shaped jump
learn.caballo-1.s0.instruction: Move the knight in an "L" to the star.
learn.caballo-1.s0.hint: The knight jumps 2 + 1 squares. Take it from b1 to c3.
learn.caballo-1.s0.comment: Well done, that is the L-shaped jump!
learn.caballo-1.s1.title: Two jumps
learn.caballo-1.s1.instruction: Capture both stars with the knight.
learn.caballo-1.s1.hint: Jump to c3 and from there to e4.
learn.caballo-1.s2.title: Three jumps
learn.caballo-1.s2.instruction: Capture all three stars with the knight.
learn.caballo-1.s2.hint: Follow the stars in order, jumping in an L.
learn.caballo-1.s3.title: The tour
learn.caballo-1.s3.instruction: Tour the board capturing every star.
learn.caballo-1.s3.hint: Each jump is an "L". Follow the stars one by one.
learn.caballo-1.s4.title: Jump over the pieces
learn.caballo-1.s4.instruction: The knight jumps over your own pawns. Capture the stars!
learn.caballo-1.s4.hint: Even if pawns surround it, the knight can jump over them.
learn.caballo-1.s5.title: The grand tour
learn.caballo-1.s5.instruction: Capture every star with the knight.
learn.caballo-1.s5.hint: Follow the stars in order; each move is an L-shaped jump.
learn.alfil-1.title: The Bishop
learn.alfil-1.desc: The bishop moves diagonally and always stays on squares of the same color. Complete the 6 exercises in order.
learn.alfil-1.success: Bishop chapter complete! It moves diagonally and always on the same color of square.
learn.alfil-1.s0.title: One diagonal
learn.alfil-1.s0.instruction: Move the bishop diagonally to the star.
learn.alfil-1.s0.hint: The bishop moves diagonally. Take it from a1 to d4.
learn.alfil-1.s1.title: Change diagonal
learn.alfil-1.s1.instruction: Capture both stars by changing diagonal.
learn.alfil-1.s1.hint: Go to e5 and then change diagonal toward b8.
learn.alfil-1.s2.title: Turn at the corners
learn.alfil-1.s2.instruction: Capture every star with the bishop.
learn.alfil-1.s2.hint: Follow the diagonals, turning at each star.
learn.alfil-1.s3.title: The tour
learn.alfil-1.s3.instruction: Tour the board capturing the stars.
learn.alfil-1.s3.hint: Change diagonal at each star to continue the tour.
learn.alfil-1.s4.title: Go around the obstacle
learn.alfil-1.s4.instruction: The pawn blocks your diagonal. Go around it to capture the stars.
learn.alfil-1.s4.hint: You cannot cross the pawn: detour via h4 and d8 to reach a5.
learn.alfil-1.s5.title: The grand tour
learn.alfil-1.s5.instruction: Capture every star with the bishop.
learn.alfil-1.s5.hint: Follow the stars in order, changing diagonal at each turn.
learn.torre-1.title: The Rook
learn.torre-1.desc: The rook moves horizontally or vertically any number of squares. Complete the 6 exercises in order.
learn.torre-1.success: Rook chapter complete! You now master the rook's movement.
learn.torre-1.s0.title: Straight line
learn.torre-1.s0.instruction: Move the rook to the star.
learn.torre-1.s0.hint: The rook goes up its file. Take it from a1 to the star on a5.
learn.torre-1.s1.title: Two stars
learn.torre-1.s1.instruction: Capture both stars with the rook.
learn.torre-1.s1.hint: Go up to a5 and then along the rank to e5.
learn.torre-1.s1.comment: Perfect, you turned at the corner!
learn.torre-1.s2.title: Turn at the corners
learn.torre-1.s2.instruction: Capture every star with the rook.
learn.torre-1.s2.hint: Go up the a-file, across the 8th rank, and down the g-file.
learn.torre-1.s3.title: The tour
learn.torre-1.s3.instruction: Capture every star with the rook.
learn.torre-1.s3.hint: Go up the a-file, across the top, down the g-file, and back along the 2nd rank.
learn.torre-1.s4.title: Go around the obstacle
learn.torre-1.s4.instruction: The pawn blocks the a-file. Go around it to capture the stars.
learn.torre-1.s4.hint: Step out to the b-file (b1), go up to b8, and enter a8 along the rank.
learn.torre-1.s5.title: The grand tour
learn.torre-1.s5.instruction: Capture every star with the rook.
learn.torre-1.s5.hint: Follow the stars in order, turning at each change of direction.
learn.dama-1.title: The Queen
learn.dama-1.desc: The queen combines the rook and the bishop: it moves in any direction. Complete the 5 exercises in order.
learn.dama-1.success: Queen chapter complete! It combines rook and bishop: up to 27 squares from the center!
learn.dama-1.s0.title: Straight line
learn.dama-1.s0.instruction: Move the queen in a straight line to the star.
learn.dama-1.s0.hint: Like the rook, the queen moves along ranks and files. Go up from a1 to a5.
learn.dama-1.s1.title: On the diagonal
learn.dama-1.s1.instruction: Move the queen diagonally to the star.
learn.dama-1.s1.hint: Like the bishop, the queen also moves diagonally: from a1 to e5.
learn.dama-1.s2.title: In every direction
learn.dama-1.s2.instruction: Capture the stars combining straight lines and diagonals.
learn.dama-1.s2.hint: Go to d4 on the diagonal, up to d8 along the file, and down to h4 on the diagonal.
learn.dama-1.s3.title: The tour
learn.dama-1.s3.instruction: Tour the board capturing the stars.
learn.dama-1.s3.hint: Follow the stars in order: the queen can reach anywhere.
learn.dama-1.s4.title: The grand tour
learn.dama-1.s4.instruction: Capture every star with the queen.
learn.dama-1.s4.hint: Combine straight and diagonal moves following the stars.
learn.rey-1.title: The King
learn.rey-1.desc: The king moves one square in any direction. Complete the 5 exercises in order.
learn.rey-1.success: King chapter complete! It moves one square in any direction: always protect it!
learn.rey-1.s0.title: One step
learn.rey-1.s0.instruction: Move the king one square to the star.
learn.rey-1.s0.hint: The king moves only one square. Take it from d1 to d2.
learn.rey-1.s1.title: Take a walk
learn.rey-1.s1.instruction: Advance the king step by step to the stars.
learn.rey-1.s1.hint: Each king move is one square.
learn.rey-1.s2.title: On the diagonal
learn.rey-1.s2.instruction: Move the king diagonally capturing the stars.
learn.rey-1.s2.hint: The king also moves diagonally, one square at a time.
learn.rey-1.s3.title: The tour
learn.rey-1.s3.instruction: Tour the board with the king following the stars.
learn.rey-1.s3.hint: Follow the stars one by one, square by square.
learn.rey-1.s4.title: The long walk
learn.rey-1.s4.instruction: Take the king along the edge capturing every star.
learn.rey-1.s4.hint: Follow the stars in order, one square at a time.
learn.basico-captura.title: Capture
learn.basico-captura.desc: Capturing enemy pieces is essential. Move to a rival piece's square to remove it from the board. Complete the 6 exercises in order.
learn.basico-captura.success: Capture chapter complete! Winning material gives a decisive advantage.
learn.basico-captura.s0.title: First capture
learn.basico-captura.s0.instruction: The rook can capture the black pawn by moving to its square.
learn.basico-captura.s0.hint: Move the rook along the d-file to the black pawn on d6.
learn.basico-captura.s0.comment: Capture! The enemy piece disappears from the board.
learn.basico-captura.s1.title: The bishop captures
learn.basico-captura.s1.instruction: The bishop captures diagonally. Capture the black pawn!
learn.basico-captura.s1.hint: The bishop on a3 moves diagonally to the pawn on d6.
learn.basico-captura.s2.title: The knight captures
learn.basico-captura.s2.instruction: The knight jumps in an L to capture the pawn.
learn.basico-captura.s2.hint: From e4 the knight jumps 2 up and 1 left: d6!
learn.basico-captura.s3.title: Two captures
learn.basico-captura.s3.instruction: The queen can capture both pawns. Start with the one on d7!
learn.basico-captura.s3.hint: The queen goes up the file to d7 and then across the rank to g7.
learn.basico-captura.s4.title: The rook harvests
learn.basico-captura.s4.instruction: The rook can capture three pawns one by one.
learn.basico-captura.s4.hint: Go up the g-file capturing on g4 and g7, then across to d7.
learn.basico-captura.s5.title: Big harvest
learn.basico-captura.s5.instruction: The rook can take all the pawns. Go get them!
learn.basico-captura.s5.hint: Go up the a-file capturing on a6 and a7, then across to b7.
learn.basico-captura.s5.comment: Big harvest! Three fewer pawns for the opponent.
learn.basico-proteccion.title: Protection
learn.basico-proteccion.desc: An undefended piece is called a "hanging piece" and can be captured for free. Learn to spot them! Complete the 6 exercises.
learn.basico-proteccion.success: Protection chapter complete! Never leave your pieces undefended.
learn.basico-proteccion.s0.title: Hanging piece
learn.basico-proteccion.s0.instruction: The black rook is undefended. Capture it!
learn.basico-proteccion.s0.hint: Your rook on e1 goes straight up to e5, where the black rook stands alone.
learn.basico-proteccion.s0.comment: An undefended piece is a gift!
learn.basico-proteccion.s1.title: The loose bishop
learn.basico-proteccion.s1.instruction: The black bishop on g5 is undefended. Capture it with your bishop!
learn.basico-proteccion.s1.hint: Your bishop on c1 reaches g5 along the diagonal.
learn.basico-proteccion.s1.comment: You captured the bishop without losing anything!
learn.basico-proteccion.s2.title: The careless queen
learn.basico-proteccion.s2.instruction: The black queen is alone on d5. Capture it with the rook!
learn.basico-proteccion.s2.hint: The rook on d1 goes up the d-file to the queen on d5.
learn.basico-proteccion.s2.comment: You captured the opponent's most valuable piece!
learn.basico-proteccion.s3.title: The loose knight
learn.basico-proteccion.s3.instruction: The black knight on d5 has no defense. Capture it with the queen!
learn.basico-proteccion.s3.hint: Your queen on d1 goes up the d-file to the knight on d5.
learn.basico-proteccion.s4.title: Clear the path
learn.basico-proteccion.s4.instruction: The black bishop on d3 blocks the path to the queen on d7. Capture the bishop first!
learn.basico-proteccion.s4.hint: The rook goes to d3 (captures the blocking bishop) and then on to d7 (captures the queen).
learn.basico-proteccion.s4.comment: You cleared the path and captured both pieces!
learn.basico-proteccion.s5.title: Two hanging pieces
learn.basico-proteccion.s5.instruction: There are two undefended black pieces on the d-file. Capture them in order!
learn.basico-proteccion.s5.hint: The rook goes to d3 (captures the bishop), then up to d6 (captures the black rook).
learn.basico-proteccion.s5.comment: Two pieces captured! Overwhelming material advantage.
learn.basico-combate.title: Combat
learn.basico-combate.desc: In combat you capture and recapture. Learn to win the exchanges! Complete the 6 exercises.
learn.basico-combate.success: Combat chapter complete! Understanding exchanges is key to winning.
learn.basico-combate.s0.title: Capture the most valuable
learn.basico-combate.s0.instruction: There is an undefended black queen. Capture it with the rook!
learn.basico-combate.s0.hint: The rook on d1 goes up to the queen on d5 along the d-file.
learn.basico-combate.s0.comment: You won the queen! That is a huge exchange in your favor.
learn.basico-combate.s1.title: Choose well
learn.basico-combate.s1.instruction: There are a black queen and rook on the 5th rank. Capture the more valuable one!
learn.basico-combate.s1.hint: The queen is worth more than the rook. Capture the queen on d5!
learn.basico-combate.s1.comment: You captured the queen, the most valuable piece!
learn.basico-combate.s2.title: Rook exchange
learn.basico-combate.s2.instruction: You can capture the black rook. Rook for rook is a fair exchange!
learn.basico-combate.s2.hint: Your rook on d1 goes up to the black rook on d5.
learn.basico-combate.s2.comment: Rook exchange! The material stays balanced.
learn.basico-combate.s3.title: Capture and harvest
learn.basico-combate.s3.instruction: Capture the black rook and then the pawn.
learn.basico-combate.s3.hint: Rook d1→d6 (captures the black rook), then think: what can the rook reach from d6?
learn.basico-combate.s4.title: Attack the most valuable first
learn.basico-combate.s4.instruction: There are a black knight and rook. Your bishop attacks the knight. Capture it!
learn.basico-combate.s4.hint: The bishop on c1 can attack the knight on e3 (diagonal), or the rook on e1 can go up to e5.
learn.basico-combate.s4.comment: Piece captured! Controlling the center gives an advantage.
learn.basico-combate.s5.title: The big exchange
learn.basico-combate.s5.instruction: Capture the black rook with the white rook, not with the queen!
learn.basico-combate.s5.hint: Use the rook (d2→d6) to capture the black rook. Save the queen for more important attacks.
learn.basico-combate.s5.comment: Good! Capture with the lower-value piece when you can.
learn.basico-jaque-1.title: Check in one
learn.basico-jaque-1.desc: Check attacks the king directly. The opponent MUST reply at once. Learn to give check! Complete the 6 exercises.
learn.basico-jaque-1.success: Check in one chapter complete! Check forces the opponent to react.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s0.title: Check with the rook
learn.basico-jaque-1.s0.instruction: Give check to the black king with the rook.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s0.hint: Move the rook to the c-file (same as the king) or to the 8th rank to give check.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s0.comment: Check! The rook attacks the king along a rank or file.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s1.title: Check with the bishop
learn.basico-jaque-1.s1.instruction: Give check to the black king with the bishop.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s1.hint: The bishop on a1 and the king on h8 are on the same diagonal. Move along it!
learn.basico-jaque-1.s1.comment: Check! The bishop attacks on the diagonal.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s2.title: Check with the queen
learn.basico-jaque-1.s2.instruction: Give check to the black king with the queen.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s2.hint: The queen can give check from the e-file, the 8th rank, or from the diagonals of e8.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s2.comment: Check with the queen! It is the most powerful piece for attacking.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s3.title: Check with the knight
learn.basico-jaque-1.s3.instruction: Give check to the black king with the knight.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s3.hint: The knight on d4 can jump to c6 or e6, from where it attacks the king on d8.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s3.comment: Check with the knight! The L-shaped jump can surprise the opponent.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s4.title: Check along the rank
learn.basico-jaque-1.s4.instruction: The black king is on e7. Give check with the rook!
learn.basico-jaque-1.s4.hint: Move the rook to any square on the e-file (same as the king on e7) to give check.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s5.title: Choose your check
learn.basico-jaque-1.s5.instruction: You have a rook and a queen. Give check to the black king!
learn.basico-jaque-1.s5.hint: The queen to e8 or any square on the e-file gives check. The rook to a8 gives check along the rank.
learn.basico-jaque-1.s5.comment: Check! With more pieces you have more attacking options.
learn.basico-jaque-2.title: Getting out of check
learn.basico-jaque-2.desc: In check you MUST get out of it. There are 3 ways: move the king, block the attack, or capture the checking piece. Complete the 5 exercises.
learn.basico-jaque-2.success: Getting out of check chapter complete! You must always answer check immediately.
learn.basico-jaque-2.s0.title: Move the king
learn.basico-jaque-2.s0.instruction: Your black king is in check from the white rook. Move it to a safe square!
learn.basico-jaque-2.s0.hint: The king can go to d8, d7, f8, or f7 to escape the check from the rook on e6.
learn.basico-jaque-2.s0.comment: Good! You escaped check by moving the king.
learn.basico-jaque-2.s1.title: Capture the attacker
learn.basico-jaque-2.s1.instruction: Your king is in check from the rook on e7. Capture it with the king!
learn.basico-jaque-2.s1.hint: The black king can capture the white rook on e7. The rook is undefended.
learn.basico-jaque-2.s1.comment: You captured the piece that was giving check!
learn.basico-jaque-2.s2.title: Block the check
learn.basico-jaque-2.s2.instruction: The black king is in check from the white rook on e1. Block with your rook!
learn.basico-jaque-2.s2.hint: Interpose your black rook on e5 between the king on e8 and the white rook on e1.
learn.basico-jaque-2.s2.comment: You blocked the check with your own rook!
learn.basico-jaque-2.s3.title: Choose the way out
learn.basico-jaque-2.s3.instruction: The black king on d8 is in check from the rook on d3. Escape!
learn.basico-jaque-2.s3.hint: The king can go to c8, c7, e8, or e7 to get out of check.
learn.basico-jaque-2.s4.title: Capture or escape
learn.basico-jaque-2.s4.instruction: Your king is in check. You can escape by moving the king or capture the white rook with your rook.
learn.basico-jaque-2.s4.hint: The black rook on e5 can capture the white rook on e1. Or the king can move.
learn.basico-mate.title: Mate in one
learn.basico-mate.desc: Checkmate wins the game at once: the attacked king cannot escape. Complete the 6 exercises.
learn.basico-mate.success: Mate in one chapter complete! Always look for checkmate before any other move.
learn.basico-mate.s0.title: Mate with the queen
learn.basico-mate.s0.instruction: There is checkmate in 1! Move the queen to trap the black king.
learn.basico-mate.s0.hint: The queen on b8 gives check and the king on a8 cannot escape: a7 and b7 are controlled by the white king.
learn.basico-mate.s0.comment: CHECKMATE! The black king has no escape.
learn.basico-mate.s1.title: Back-rank mate
learn.basico-mate.s1.instruction: The black king is trapped behind its own pawns! Mate with the rook.
learn.basico-mate.s1.hint: Take the rook to d8: the king on g8 cannot escape because its own pawns block the way out.
learn.basico-mate.s1.comment: Back-rank mate! Your own pawns can become the king's prison.
learn.basico-mate.s2.title: Box mate
learn.basico-mate.s2.instruction: Give checkmate to the black king with the rook!
learn.basico-mate.s2.hint: The rook on b8 gives check and the king on a8 cannot go to a7 (white king on a6) or b7 (rook).
learn.basico-mate.s2.comment: Box mate! The rook and king together trap the enemy king.
learn.basico-mate.s3.title: Ladder mate
learn.basico-mate.s3.instruction: There is mate in 1 with the rook! Can you find it?
learn.basico-mate.s3.hint: The rook to b8 gives check. The king on a8 cannot go to a7 or b7 (both controlled by the king on b6).
learn.basico-mate.s3.comment: Ladder mate! The ladder technique is fundamental in endgames.
learn.basico-mate.s4.title: Mate with the queen (corner)
learn.basico-mate.s4.instruction: There is mate in 1 with the queen!
learn.basico-mate.s4.hint: The queen on b7 gives check and the king on b8 cannot escape with the white king on b6. c8 also works.
learn.basico-mate.s4.comment: Checkmate with the queen! It covers every flight square.
learn.basico-mate.s5.title: Mate with two rooks
learn.basico-mate.s5.instruction: The two rooks give mate in 1! Which one do you move?
learn.basico-mate.s5.hint: The rook to a1 gives check along the a-file. The king on a8 cannot go to b8 (rook on b7) or a7 (the rook on b7 covers a7).
learn.basico-mate.s5.comment: Mate with two rooks! Rook coordination is devastating.
learn.inter-tablero.title: Setting up the board
learn.inter-tablero.desc: Learn where each piece starts. Rank 1 belongs to White and the queen goes on her own color. Complete the 6 exercises.
learn.inter-tablero.success: Setting up the board chapter complete! Rook, knight, bishop, queen on her color, and king beside her.
learn.inter-tablero.s0.title: The rooks
learn.inter-tablero.s0.instruction: The rooks start in the corners. Take the rook to its starting square.
learn.inter-tablero.s0.hint: Move the rook from b1 to the corner a1.
learn.inter-tablero.s0.comment: Good! The rooks start on a1 and h1.
learn.inter-tablero.s1.title: The knights
learn.inter-tablero.s1.instruction: The knights stand next to the rooks. Take the knight to its starting square.
learn.inter-tablero.s1.hint: Jump with the knight from c3 to b1.
learn.inter-tablero.s1.comment: Good! The knights start on b1 and g1.
learn.inter-tablero.s2.title: The bishops
learn.inter-tablero.s2.instruction: The bishops stand next to the knights. Take the bishop to its starting square.
learn.inter-tablero.s2.hint: Move the bishop diagonally from a3 to c1.
learn.inter-tablero.s2.comment: Good! The bishops start on c1 and f1.
learn.inter-tablero.s3.title: The queen on her color
learn.inter-tablero.s3.instruction: The white queen starts on a light square: d1. Place her!
learn.inter-tablero.s3.hint: Bring the queen down the d-file to d1. Remember: "queen on her color".
learn.inter-tablero.s3.comment: Good! White queen on a light square (d1), black queen on a dark square (d8).
learn.inter-tablero.s4.title: The king
learn.inter-tablero.s4.instruction: The king takes the remaining square next to the queen: e1.
learn.inter-tablero.s4.hint: Move the king from e2 to e1.
learn.inter-tablero.s4.comment: Good! The white king starts on e1 and the black king on e8.
learn.inter-tablero.s5.title: First move
learn.inter-tablero.s5.instruction: The board is set (the pawns occupy the whole 2nd rank). Make your first move!
learn.inter-tablero.s5.hint: Any legal move is fine. The classics are e4 or d4.
learn.inter-enroque.title: Castling
learn.inter-enroque.desc: Castling tucks the king away and activates the rook: the king moves 2 squares toward the rook and the rook jumps to the other side. Complete the 5 exercises.
learn.inter-enroque.success: Castling chapter complete! You cannot castle if the king or rook has already moved, nor through attacked squares.
learn.inter-enroque.s0.title: Kingside castling
learn.inter-enroque.s0.instruction: Castle kingside: move the king 2 squares toward the rook on h1.
learn.inter-enroque.s0.hint: Click the king (e1) and then g1. The rook will jump automatically to f1.
learn.inter-enroque.s0.comment: Kingside castling! The king is on g1 and the rook on f1.
learn.inter-enroque.s1.title: Queenside castling
learn.inter-enroque.s1.instruction: Castle queenside: move the king 2 squares toward the rook on a1.
learn.inter-enroque.s1.hint: Click the king (e1) and then c1. The rook will jump automatically to d1.
learn.inter-enroque.s1.comment: Queenside castling! The king is on c1 and the rook on d1.
learn.inter-enroque.s2.title: Choose your castling
learn.inter-enroque.s2.instruction: You can castle on either side. Choose!
learn.inter-enroque.s2.hint: Move the king to g1 (kingside) or to c1 (queenside).
learn.inter-enroque.s3.title: Attacked square
learn.inter-enroque.s3.instruction: The black bishop attacks f1: the king cannot pass through an attacked square. Castle on the safe side!
learn.inter-enroque.s3.hint: Kingside castling is illegal because the king would pass through f1, attacked by the bishop on a6. Castle queenside (e1 → c1).
learn.inter-enroque.s3.comment: Good! The king can never pass through an attacked square when castling.
learn.inter-enroque.s4.title: Castle early
learn.inter-enroque.s4.instruction: In the opening it is wise to castle as soon as possible to protect the king. Castle kingside!
learn.inter-enroque.s4.hint: Squares f1 and g1 are already free: move the king from e1 to g1.
learn.inter-enroque.s4.comment: King safe and rook active! A great opening principle.
learn.inter-alpaso.title: En passant
learn.inter-alpaso.desc: If an enemy pawn advances 2 squares and lands beside yours, you can capture it en passant as if it had moved only 1. Complete the 4 exercises.
learn.inter-alpaso.success: En passant chapter complete! Remember: it is only possible on the turn immediately after the 2-square advance.
learn.inter-alpaso.s0.title: En passant
learn.inter-alpaso.s0.instruction: The black pawn has just advanced 2 squares (d7-d5). Capture it en passant!
learn.inter-alpaso.s0.hint: Move your pawn from e5 to d6: the black pawn on d5 disappears.
learn.inter-alpaso.s0.comment: En passant! The pawn is captured as if it had advanced only one square.
learn.inter-alpaso.s1.title: Only the last one
learn.inter-alpaso.s1.instruction: The f-pawn has just advanced 2 squares; the d-pawn did so several turns ago. You can only capture the last one en passant. Capture on f6!
learn.inter-alpaso.s1.hint: En passant is only legal right after the 2-square advance: e5 → f6.
learn.inter-alpaso.s1.comment: Exactly! En passant only captures the pawn that has JUST advanced two squares.
learn.inter-alpaso.s2.title: Choose the side
learn.inter-alpaso.s2.instruction: The black pawn advanced 2 squares between your two pawns. Either one can capture it en passant!
learn.inter-alpaso.s2.hint: Capture on e6 with the pawn on d5 or the one on f5.
learn.inter-alpaso.s2.comment: Captured! Both pawns were watching e6.
learn.inter-alpaso.s3.title: No escape
learn.inter-alpaso.s3.instruction: The black pawn tried to slip past by advancing 2 squares. Capture it en passant!
learn.inter-alpaso.s3.hint: Move your pawn from b5 to a6 to capture en passant.
learn.inter-alpaso.s3.comment: Good! Advancing two squares does not dodge an enemy pawn.
learn.inter-ahogado.title: Stalemate
learn.inter-ahogado.desc: If the opponent is not in check but has no legal move, the game ends in a draw by stalemate. Practice forcing it! Complete the 4 exercises.
learn.inter-ahogado.success: Stalemate chapter complete! Stalemate = draw: force it if you are losing and avoid it if you are winning.
learn.inter-ahogado.s0.title: Stalemate with the queen
learn.inter-ahogado.s0.instruction: Leave the black king with no legal moves but WITHOUT giving check. Move the queen to c7.
learn.inter-ahogado.s0.hint: The queen on c7 covers a7, b7, and b8, but does NOT attack a8: the king is stalemated.
learn.inter-ahogado.s0.comment: Stalemate! The king is not in check and cannot move: draw.
learn.inter-ahogado.s1.title: The corner
learn.inter-ahogado.s1.instruction: The black king is in the h1 corner. Stalemate it with the queen!
learn.inter-ahogado.s1.hint: The queen on f2 covers g1, g2, and h2 without giving check to h1.
learn.inter-ahogado.s1.comment: Stalemate in the corner! Careful: with the queen it is very easy to stalemate by accident.
learn.inter-ahogado.s2.title: The promoting pawn
learn.inter-ahogado.s2.instruction: Come closer with the king to support the pawn… and stalemate the black king!
learn.inter-ahogado.s2.hint: With your king on g6, the black king cannot go to g7, g8, or capture on h7: stalemate.
learn.inter-ahogado.s2.comment: Stalemate! This king-and-rook-pawn position is a classic draw.
learn.inter-ahogado.s3.title: Stalemate with the rook
learn.inter-ahogado.s3.instruction: Stalemate the black king with the rook (no check!).
learn.inter-ahogado.s3.hint: The rook on b7 covers a7 and b8 and is defended by your king: stalemate.
learn.inter-ahogado.s3.comment: Stalemate! In a winning endgame this would be a mistake: avoid stalemate when you are winning.
learn.av-valor.title: Piece values
learn.av-valor.desc: Pawn 1 · Knight 3 · Bishop 3 · Rook 5 · Queen 9. When you can choose, capture the higher-value piece. Complete the 5 exercises.
learn.av-valor.success: Piece values chapter complete! Queen 9, Rook 5, Bishop and Knight 3, Pawn 1: always capture the most valuable… if it is safe.
learn.av-valor.s0.title: Rook or knight
learn.av-valor.s0.instruction: Your queen can capture the rook or the knight. Capture the more valuable piece!
learn.av-valor.s0.hint: The rook is worth 5 points and the knight 3. Take the queen up the d-file to d7.
learn.av-valor.s1.title: Rook or knight II
learn.av-valor.s1.instruction: Again you can choose between rook and knight. Choose well!
learn.av-valor.s1.hint: The queen reaches the rook on a8 along the diagonal.
learn.av-valor.s1.comment: Rook captured! 5 points are worth more than 3.
learn.av-valor.s2.title: Watch the defense!
learn.av-valor.s2.instruction: The rook on d7 is defended by its king: capturing it loses the queen. Capture the bishop for free!
learn.av-valor.s2.hint: If you take the rook, the king recaptures your queen (9 for 5 = a bad deal). The bishop on h5 is undefended.
learn.av-valor.s2.comment: Exactly! Value only counts if the capture is safe.
learn.av-valor.s3.title: Bishop or pawn
learn.av-valor.s3.instruction: Your rook can capture the bishop or the pawn. Capture the more valuable piece!
learn.av-valor.s3.hint: The bishop is worth 3 points and the pawn only 1. Move the rook along the first rank to f1.
learn.av-valor.s4.title: The winning jump
learn.av-valor.s4.instruction: Your knight can capture the rook or the pawn. Choose the more valuable one!
learn.av-valor.s4.hint: Jump with the knight from d5 to e7 to capture the rook (5 points).
learn.av-valor.s4.comment: Rook captured! The knight reaches surprising squares.
learn.av-jaque2.title: Check in two
learn.av-jaque2.desc: Sometimes check needs preparation: one move to get into position and another to attack the king. Complete the 4 exercises (2 moves each).
learn.av-jaque2.success: Check in two chapter complete! Always think of a preparing move before the blow.
learn.av-jaque2.s0.title: Lift the rook
learn.av-jaque2.s0.instruction: No move gives check yet. Lift the rook to a6 to prepare the attack.
learn.av-jaque2.s0.hint: The rook on a6 will then be able to slide along the 6th rank toward the king.
learn.av-jaque2.s0.comment: Rook activated! Now comes the check.
learn.av-jaque2.s1.title: Finish with the rook
learn.av-jaque2.s1.instruction: Now slide the rook along the 6th rank and give check to the king.
learn.av-jaque2.s1.hint: The rook on e6 attacks the king on e8 along the e-file.
learn.av-jaque2.s2.title: Aim with the bishop
learn.av-jaque2.s2.instruction: The bishop cannot give check yet. Take it to a3 to aim at f8.
learn.av-jaque2.s2.hint: From a3, the bishop controls the a3–f8 diagonal, next to the black king.
learn.av-jaque2.s3.title: Fire the bishop
learn.av-jaque2.s3.instruction: Now slide the bishop along the diagonal and give check.
learn.av-jaque2.s3.hint: The bishop on f8 attacks the king on g7.
learn.av-jaque2.s4.title: Bring the knight closer
learn.av-jaque2.s4.instruction: The knight is far away. Jump to e4 to approach the king.
learn.av-jaque2.s4.hint: From e4 the knight will reach d6 or f6, from where it will give check.
learn.av-jaque2.s5.title: Jump with check
learn.av-jaque2.s5.instruction: Now jump and give check to the black king. There are two options!
learn.av-jaque2.s5.hint: The knight gives check to e8 from d6 or from f6.
learn.av-jaque2.s5.comment: Check with the knight in two jumps!
learn.av-jaque2.s6.title: Infiltrate the queen
learn.av-jaque2.s6.instruction: The black rook on e8 prevents check on the 8th rank. Take the queen to d8 to attack it.
learn.av-jaque2.s6.hint: The queen goes up the d-file to d8, attacking the rook on e8.
learn.av-jaque2.s6.comment: Rook attacked! And it is undefended…
learn.av-jaque2.s7.title: Strike with the queen
learn.av-jaque2.s7.instruction: Capture the rook and give check to the king at the same time!
learn.av-jaque2.s7.hint: The queen captures the rook on e8: check to the king on g8 along the 8th rank.
learn.av-jaque2.s7.comment: Check and rook captured! Preparing the attack in two moves is the basis of tactics.
learn.jaque-1.title: Giving Check with the Rook
learn.jaque-1.desc: Check occurs when the king is attacked directly. The player in check must get out of it immediately. The rook attacks along ranks and files.
learn.jaque-1.success: Lesson complete! The rook gives check by attacking the king on the same rank or file.
learn.jaque-1.s0.instruction: Give check to the black king by moving the rook to its same rank.
learn.jaque-1.s0.hint: Move the rook to f6: it will be on the same rank as the black king on e6.
learn.jaque-1.s0.comment: Check! The black king is under attack.
learn.jaque-2.title: Escaping Check
learn.jaque-2.desc: When your king is in check you MUST get out of it. There are 3 ways: move the king, block the attack, or capture the checking piece.
learn.jaque-2.success: Lesson complete! To get out of check you can move the king, block, or capture.
learn.jaque-2.s0.instruction: Your black king is in check from the white rook. Save it!
learn.jaque-2.s0.hint: The king can move to d5, d6, d7, e7, f5, f6, f7, or capture the rook on e5.
learn.jaque-3.title: Discovered Check
learn.jaque-3.desc: Discovered check occurs when you move a piece and another that was behind it is left attacking the enemy king.
learn.jaque-3.success: Lesson complete! Discovered check can be very surprising for the opponent.
learn.jaque-3.s0.instruction: Move the bishop off the a-file so the rook discovers check on the black king.
learn.jaque-3.s0.hint: Move the bishop diagonally: when it leaves the a-file, the rook will attack the king on a8.
learn.jaque-3.s0.comment: Discovered check! The rook now attacks the black king.
learn.mate-1.title: Checkmate with the Queen
learn.mate-1.desc: Checkmate is a check from which the king cannot escape. It is the goal of chess!
learn.mate-1.success: Lesson complete! Checkmate wins the game instantly.
learn.mate-1.s0.instruction: There is checkmate in 1! Move the queen so the king has no escape.
learn.mate-1.s0.hint: The queen on b8 gives check and the king on a8 cannot escape. The white king on b6 covers a7 and b7.
learn.mate-1.s0.comment: Checkmate! The black king has no escape.
learn.mate-2.title: Back-Rank Mate
learn.mate-2.desc: Back-rank mate occurs when the enemy king is trapped behind its own pawns and cannot escape the rook's attack.
learn.mate-2.success: Lesson complete! Back-rank mate is very common in real games. Protect your king!
learn.mate-2.s0.instruction: Mate the black king by taking the rook to the last rank.
learn.mate-2.s0.hint: Move the rook to d8: the king on g8 cannot escape because its own pawns block the way out.
learn.mate-2.s0.comment: Back-rank checkmate! The black pawns are to blame.
learn.mate-3.title: Mate with 2 Rooks
learn.mate-3.desc: Two coordinated rooks can deliver mate systematically. One gives check and the other cuts off the king's flight.
learn.mate-3.success: Lesson complete! With two rooks you can mate any king with the right technique.
learn.mate-3.s0.instruction: Move the second rook to give checkmate to the king on a8.
learn.mate-3.s0.hint: The rook on a1 gives check. The king cannot go to b8 (rook on b7) or a7 (rook on b7). It is mate!
learn.mate-3.s0.comment: Checkmate! The two coordinated rooks trap the king.
learn.horquilla.title: The Fork
learn.horquilla.desc: A fork is a simultaneous attack on two or more pieces with a single piece. The knight is the king of forks thanks to its "L" move.
learn.horquilla.success: Lesson complete! The knight fork is a very powerful tactic.
learn.horquilla.s0.instruction: Move the knight to attack the black king and the black rook at the same time. Look for the fork!
learn.horquilla.s0.hint: The knight on c7 attacks both the king on e8 and the rook on a8.
learn.horquilla.s0.comment: Fork! The knight attacks the king and the rook at the same time.
learn.horquilla.s1.instruction: The king has escaped check, but the rook is still hanging! Capture it!
learn.horquilla.s1.hint: The knight on c7 can capture the rook on a8.
learn.horquilla.s1.comment: Excellent! You won a rook with the fork.
learn.clavada.title: The Pin
learn.clavada.desc: A pin immobilizes a piece because if it moves, it would leave the king in check or lose a more valuable piece. The pinned piece cannot move freely.
learn.clavada.success: Lesson complete! Always look for the opponent's pinned pieces to attack them.
learn.clavada.s0.instruction: The black rook is pinned: it cannot move without leaving the king in check. Capture it!
learn.clavada.s0.hint: Move the white rook from e2 to e7 to capture the pinned rook.
learn.clavada.s0.comment: Correct! You captured the pinned piece.
learn.colgante.title: Hanging Piece
learn.colgante.desc: A piece is "hanging" when it is not defended by any enemy piece. You can capture it without losing material.
learn.colgante.success: Lesson complete! Before you move, always check whether the opponent has hanging pieces.
learn.colgante.s0.instruction: The black rook is hanging (undefended). Capture it with the queen!
learn.colgante.s0.hint: Move the queen from d1 to d3 to capture the undefended black rook.
learn.colgante.s0.comment: Perfect! You won a rook for free.
learn.ej-caballo.title: Knight's Tour
learn.ej-caballo.desc: Practice the knight's "L" jump by touring the board and capturing every star in order.
learn.ej-caballo.success: Exercise complete! You master the knight's "L" move.
learn.ej-caballo.s0.instruction: Capture every star with the knight.
learn.ej-caballo.s0.hint: The knight jumps in an "L". Capture each star in the order they appear.
learn.ej-alfil.title: Bishop Diagonals
learn.ej-alfil.desc: The bishop always moves diagonally on squares of the same color. Capture every star.
learn.ej-alfil.success: Exercise complete! The bishop dominates the board's diagonals.
learn.ej-alfil.s0.instruction: Capture every star with the bishop.
learn.ej-alfil.s0.hint: The bishop moves diagonally. Follow the stars along the diagonals.
learn.ej-dama.title: Grand Queen Tour
learn.ej-dama.desc: The queen combines rook and bishop: it moves in a straight line and diagonally. Capture every star.
learn.ej-dama.success: Exercise complete! The queen is the most versatile and powerful piece.
learn.ej-dama.s0.instruction: Capture every star with the queen.
learn.ej-dama.s0.hint: The queen moves in any direction. Combine straight lines and diagonals.
learn.ej-rey.title: King's Path
learn.ej-rey.desc: The king moves only one square at a time, in any direction. Capture every star step by step.
learn.ej-rey.success: Exercise complete! The king moves carefully, one square at a time.
learn.ej-rey.s0.instruction: Capture every star with the king, one square at a time.
learn.ej-rey.s0.hint: The king advances only 1 square. Approach each star step by step.
op.italiana.name: Italian Game (Giuoco Piano)
op.italiana.desc: Seeks central control and rapid development aiming at the weak f7-square. Open play with tactical chances for both sides.
op.española.name: Ruy Lopez (Spanish Opening)
op.española.desc: Pressures the knight that defends e5, looking for a long-term positional edge. The deepest and most studied opening in chess.
op.escocesa.name: Scotch Game
op.escocesa.desc: Opens the center at once, seeking active piece play and free diagonals for the bishops.
op.petrov.name: Petrov Defence
op.petrov.desc: A symmetrical, solid defence. Black counterattacks the e4-pawn instead of defending e5, looking for quick equality.
op.vienesa.name: Vienna Game
op.vienesa.desc: Prepares f4 without blocking the f-pawn. Combines King's Gambit ideas with flexible knight development.
op.gambito-rey.name: King's Gambit
op.gambito-rey.desc: Sacrifices a pawn for initiative and an attack on the king. A romantic, aggressive opening that seeks to open the f-file.
op.gambito-evans.name: Evans Gambit
op.gambito-evans.desc: Sacrifices a flank pawn to gain development tempi and build a strong center with c3 and d4.
op.dos-caballos.name: Two Knights Defence
op.dos-caballos.desc: A direct counterattack on the e4-pawn. Black prefers activity to solidity, accepting tactical complications.
op.siciliana.name: Sicilian Defence
op.siciliana.desc: The most popular and combative defence against 1.e4. Black fights for the center with a flank pawn, creating asymmetrical, tactically rich positions.
op.siciliana-najdorf.name: Najdorf Sicilian
op.siciliana-najdorf.desc: The most popular Sicilian variation. ...a6 prepares ...e5 or ...b5 for queenside counterplay while keeping flexibility.
op.siciliana-dragon.name: Dragon Sicilian
op.siciliana-dragon.desc: Fianchetto of the bishop on g7 creating pressure on the long diagonal. Leads to opposite-side attacks: White on the king, Black on the queenside.
op.siciliana-sveshnikov.name: Sveshnikov Sicilian
op.siciliana-sveshnikov.desc: An aggressive central strike that drives the knight away. Accepts a weakness on d5 in return for active play and dynamic counterplay.
op.siciliana-clasica.name: Classical Sicilian
op.siciliana-clasica.desc: Natural knight development pressing d4. A flexible position that can transpose into many systems.
op.siciliana-alapin.name: Alapin Sicilian
op.siciliana-alapin.desc: White prepares d4 reinforced by c3. Avoids the theoretical complexity of the Open Sicilian in exchange for a solid center.
op.siciliana-smith-morra.name: Smith-Morra Gambit
op.siciliana-smith-morra.desc: An aggressive gambit that sacrifices a pawn for rapid development, open files, and a strong initiative.
op.francesa.name: French Defence
op.francesa.desc: A solid defence that builds a sturdy pawn chain. Black accepts a passive bishop on c8 in return for a solid structure and a central counterattack.
op.francesa-winawer.name: French Winawer
op.francesa-winawer.desc: Pins the knight that defends e4. Leads to unbalanced play with doubled pawns and attacks on opposite flanks.
op.francesa-clasica.name: Classical French
op.francesa-clasica.desc: Direct pressure on e4. More solid play than the Winawer, with strategic plans of breaking with ...c5 or ...f6.
op.francesa-avance.name: French Advance
op.francesa-avance.desc: Fixes the pawn structure and gains space. Black looks to break with ...c5 and pressure White's pawn chain.
op.francesa-tarrasch.name: French Tarrasch
op.francesa-tarrasch.desc: Avoids the Winawer pin. Quieter play that allows recapturing on e4 with the knight, keeping the structure intact.
op.caro-kann.name: Caro-Kann Defence
op.caro-kann.desc: A solid, positional defence that seeks quick equality. Black keeps a healthy pawn structure and an active light-squared bishop.
op.caro-kann-clasica.name: Classical Caro-Kann
op.caro-kann-clasica.desc: A solid defence that develops the queen's bishop before closing the position. Seeks equality with a healthy pawn structure.
op.caro-kann-avance.name: Caro-Kann Advance
op.caro-kann-avance.desc: Gains space in the center. Black looks for counterplay with ...c5 and ...Bf5, pressing the pawn chain.
op.escandinava.name: Scandinavian Defence
op.escandinava.desc: Challenges e4 immediately. The queen comes out early but Black gets rapid development of the queen's bishop and a solid structure.
op.pirc.name: Pirc Defence
op.pirc.desc: Hypermodern: allows White to build a big center and then attacks it with ...e5 or ...c5 and the fianchettoed bishop.
op.gda.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
op.gda.desc: Black takes the gambit pawn and later gives it back, gaining tempi to develop the queen's bishop actively.
op.gdr-ortodoxa.name: QGD Orthodox
op.gdr-ortodoxa.desc: A classical system where White pressures the center with developed pieces. Deep positional play and strategic maneuvering.
op.eslava.name: Slav Defence
op.eslava.desc: Defends d5 with c6 without blocking the queen's bishop. A solid structure with plans of queenside counterplay.
op.semi-eslava.name: Semi-Slav
op.semi-eslava.desc: Combines the solidity of the Slav with the flexibility of the French. Positions rich in plans and tactical complications.
op.india-rey.name: King's Indian
op.india-rey.desc: Black allows a strong White center and then attacks it with ...e5. The bishop on g7 is a key piece for the counterattack.
op.nimzo-india.name: Nimzo-Indian
op.nimzo-india.desc: Pins the c3-knight that controls e4. Doubles White's pawns and gains positional control in return for the bishop pair.
op.india-dama.name: Queen's Indian
op.india-dama.desc: Fianchetto of the queen's bishop to control the e4-a8 diagonal. Flexible play with pressure on White's center.
op.benoni.name: Modern Benoni
op.benoni.desc: Creates asymmetry with facing pawns. Black looks for queenside counterplay with ...b5 and pressure on the c-file.
op.budapest.name: Budapest Gambit
op.budapest.desc: A surprise gambit that sacrifices a pawn for active development. The knight goes to g4 or e4 creating immediate threats.
op.holandesa.name: Dutch Defence
op.holandesa.desc: Aggressive control of the e4-square. Black looks for a kingside attack, with plans of ...Nf6, ...e6, and ...g5.
op.londres.name: London System
op.londres.desc: A universal, solid system. White builds a structure with Bf4, e3, Nf3, Bd3, and c3 against any defence.
op.colle.name: Colle System
op.colle.desc: A quiet system that seeks the e3-e4 break prepared with Bd3 and Nbd2. Ideal for positional players.
op.inglesa.name: English Opening
op.inglesa.desc: A reversed Sicilian with an extra tempo. Control of the center from the flanks with plans of g3, Bg2, and pressure on the c-file.
op.reti.name: Réti Opening
op.reti.desc: Hypermodern: attacks the center from the flank. Flexible, it can transpose into the English, Catalan, or Queen's Gambit.
op.catalana.name: Catalan Opening
op.catalana.desc: Fianchetto of the king's bishop that pressures the long a8-h1 diagonal. Combines positional solidity with persistent pressure.
op.larsen.name: Larsen's Opening
op.larsen.desc: Early fianchetto of the queen's bishop. A flexible, lightly theoretical opening that seeks long-range control of the center.
op.italiana-pianissimo.name: Giuoco Pianissimo (Tabiya)
op.italiana-pianissimo.desc: Slow, strategic play. White prepares d4 with c3 while keeping central tension. Piece maneuvers and long-term plans.
op.gambito-evans-deep.name: Evans Gambit Accepted
op.gambito-evans-deep.desc: After the pawn sacrifice, White builds a dominant center with c3+d4 and rapid development with a strong initiative.
op.española-cerrada.name: Closed Ruy Lopez (Tabiya)
op.española-cerrada.desc: A tabiya position where the plan is chosen: Breyer (Nb8), Chigorin (Na5), or Zaitsev (Bb7). Deep strategic play.
op.española-breyer.name: Ruy Lopez Breyer
op.española-breyer.desc: Repositioning the knight via b8-d7 to reinforce the center. A modern, flexible idea that prepares ...Bb7 and ...c5.
op.española-chigorin.name: Ruy Lopez Chigorin
op.española-chigorin.desc: Na5 aims to occupy c4 and pressure the queenside. With ...c5 Black generates central counterplay against d4.
op.española-marshall.name: Marshall Gambit
op.española-marshall.desc: A pawn gambit for a direct attack on the king. Black gets active pieces, open files, and a strong initiative.
op.española-berlinesa.name: Berlin: Berlin Wall
op.española-berlinesa.desc: Leads to a queenless technical endgame. Black has the bishop pair and doubled pawns but a solid structure.
op.petrov-deep.name: Classical Petrov
op.petrov-deep.desc: A symmetrical position where White keeps a slight space advantage. Technical play with precise maneuvers.
op.najdorf-ag5.name: Najdorf 6.Bg5 (Poisoned Pawn)
op.najdorf-ag5.desc: Poisoned Pawn variation: Qb6 threatens b2. Extremely complex and tactical, a favorite of Fischer and Kasparov.
op.najdorf-ae3.name: Najdorf 6.Be3
op.najdorf-ae3.desc: The modern English Attack against the Najdorf. White looks for positional play with f3, Qd2, and queenside castling.
op.dragon-yugoslavo.name: Yugoslav Dragon
op.dragon-yugoslavo.desc: Opposite-side castling with mutual attacks. White throws the kingside pawns (h4-h5) while Black attacks with ...a5-a4.
op.sveshnikov-deep.name: Sveshnikov Ndb5
op.sveshnikov-deep.desc: A fight for the d5-square. Black accepts structural weaknesses in return for active pieces and dynamic counterplay.
op.winawer-deep.name: Winawer with Qg4
op.winawer-deep.desc: A direct attack on the kingside. Black must choose between protecting g7 or castling queenside, leading to unbalanced play.
op.francesa-clasica-deep.name: Classical French McCutcheon
op.francesa-clasica-deep.desc: After the exchanges, Black looks to break with ...c5 and ...f6. A closed position with strategic play around the pawn chain.
op.francesa-avance-deep.name: French Advance with Qb6
op.francesa-avance-deep.desc: Qb6 pressures b2 and d4 at once. White reinforces with a3 and tries to keep the pawn chain intact.
op.caro-kann-deep.name: Classical Caro-Kann with h4
op.caro-kann-deep.desc: h4 gains space and threatens h5 trapping the bishop. Black must play ...h6 preventively, creating potential weaknesses.
op.caro-kann-avance-deep.name: Caro-Kann Advance with Be2
op.caro-kann-avance-deep.desc: A quiet system where White looks to keep the space advantage. Black prepares ...c5 to break the chain.
op.gdr-ortodoxa-deep.name: QGD Orthodox (Tabiya)
op.gdr-ortodoxa-deep.desc: The Orthodox tabiya. Black frees the position with ...dxc4 and looks to equalize with ...e5 or ...c5.
op.eslava-checa.name: Czech Slav with Bf5
op.eslava-checa.desc: Black captures on c4 and develops the bishop to f5 before playing ...e6. a4 prevents ...b5, defending the extra pawn.
op.semi-eslava-meran.name: Semi-Slav Meran
op.semi-eslava-meran.desc: Aggressive counterplay with ...b5 gaining space on the queenside. Black looks to activate the queen's bishop and apply pressure.
op.india-rey-clasica.name: Classical King's Indian
op.india-rey-clasica.desc: A tabiya position. Black chooses between Nc6 (Mar del Plata), Na6 (Modern), or Nd7 (Gligoric) according to the desired attacking plan.
op.india-rey-mar-plata.name: King's Indian Mar del Plata
op.india-rey-mar-plata.desc: The most combative King's Indian variation. Opposite-flank attacks: White with c5 on the queenside, Black with f5 on the kingside.
op.india-rey-samisch.name: King's Indian Sämisch
op.india-rey-samisch.desc: f3 reinforces e4 and prepares queenside castling with a kingside attack. Aggressive play where both sides attack without restraint.
op.nimzo-rubinstein.name: Nimzo-Indian Rubinstein
op.nimzo-rubinstein.desc: Black pressures d4 with ...c5 and ...d5. If bxc3, White has the bishop pair but doubled pawns.
op.nimzo-clasica.name: Classical Nimzo-Indian Qc2
op.nimzo-clasica.desc: Qc2 avoids doubled pawns. White gets the bishop pair and a strong center; Black gets good development.
op.benoni-deep.name: Classical Benoni Fianchetto
op.benoni-deep.desc: Fianchetto of the bishop to pressure d5 and e4. Black looks for counterplay with ...b5 and activity on the e-file.
op.londres-deep.name: London Main Line
op.londres-deep.desc: A solid structure with Bf4+e3+c3+Nf3. White looks for Bd3, Nbd2, and eventually e4 to gain a space advantage.
op.inglesa-4caballos.name: English Four Knights
op.inglesa-4caballos.desc: A symmetrical position with central tension. White looks to exploit the fianchetto and pressure on the c-file.
op.catalana-abierta.name: Open Catalan
op.catalana-abierta.desc: Black captures on c4 and defends with ...a6. The bishop on g2 exerts constant pressure on the diagonal, looking to recover the pawn.
op.catalana-cerrada.name: Closed Catalan
op.catalana-cerrada.desc: Black keeps the tension in the center without capturing on c4. Deep positional play with subtle strategic maneuvers.
op.alekhine.name: Alekhine Defence
op.alekhine.desc: Hypermodern: provokes the advance of White's pawns and then attacks the overextended center. The knight maneuvers while Black undermines the chain.
op.alekhine-4peones.name: Alekhine Four Pawns
op.alekhine-4peones.desc: White occupies the center with four pawns. An imposing but potentially overextended center; Black looks to undermine it.
op.alekhine-moderna.name: Modern Alekhine
op.alekhine-moderna.desc: The most flexible and popular line: natural development without committing the structure. Black chooses between ...Bg4, ...g6, or ...c6.
op.grunfeld.name: Grünfeld Defence
op.grunfeld.desc: A counterattack on White's center from the fianchetto. After cxd5 Nxd5, e4 the knight jumps and Bg7 pressures the center.
op.grunfeld-cambio.name: Grünfeld: Exchange Variation
op.grunfeld-cambio.desc: White gets a strong center with pawns on c3-d4-e4. Bg7 pressures the diagonal and Black looks to break with ...c5.
op.grunfeld-rusa.name: Grünfeld: Russian System
op.grunfeld-rusa.desc: The queen pressures d5 and b7 at once. Black must reply accurately: ...dxc4, ...c6, or ...e6 are the main options.
op.philidor.name: Philidor Defence
op.philidor.desc: A solid but passive defence. Black holds the center with ...d6 and looks for counterplay with ...Nbd7 and ...Be7.
op.philidor-hanham.name: Philidor: Hanham Variation
op.philidor-hanham.desc: Black prepares ...Be7 and ...O-O while keeping e5 protected. A flexible structure that allows ...c6 and a later break with ...d5.
op.trompowsky.name: Trompowsky Attack
op.trompowsky.desc: Pins the knight before Black defines the structure. Avoids Nimzo and King's Indian theory, looking for independent play.
op.torre.name: Torre Attack
op.torre.desc: An aggressive system that pins the knight and pressures Black's position. Popular at club level, with plans of Nbd2, e3, and c3.
op.bird.name: Bird's Opening
op.bird.desc: A flank opening that controls e5. It can transpose into a Dutch with colors reversed. Original, lightly theoretical play.
op.cuatro-caballos.name: Four Knights
op.cuatro-caballos.desc: Symmetrical knight development. A solid position with the option of transposing into the Ruy Lopez (4.Bb5) or Scotch (4.d4).
op.siciliana-kan.name: Kan Sicilian
op.siciliana-kan.desc: Flexible and solid. ...a6 prepares ...b5 and ...Bb7 without committing the structure. Allows a choice between plans with ...d6, ...Qc7, or ...b5.
op.siciliana-taimanov.name: Taimanov Sicilian
op.siciliana-taimanov.desc: Natural knight development pressing d4. A flexible position with plans of ...Qc7, ...a6, ...Ne5 according to White's reply.
op.siciliana-scheveningen.name: Scheveningen Sicilian
op.siciliana-scheveningen.desc: A structure with pawns on d6+e6, solid and flexible. Black can adapt with ...a6 (Najdorf), ...Be7, or ...Nc6 depending on the game.
op.moderna.name: Modern Defence
op.moderna.desc: Hypermodern: lets White occupy the center in order to attack it later with ...d6, ...c5, and the powerful bishop on g7.
op.bogo-india.name: Bogo-Indian
op.bogo-india.desc: A bishop check that forces White to choose: Nbd2, Bd2, or Nd2. A solid alternative to the Nimzo-Indian when 3.Nc3 is not played.
op.gambito-rey-aceptado.name: King's Gambit Accepted
op.gambito-rey-aceptado.desc: Black accepts the pawn and White looks to recover it with rapid development. Open, tactical, aggressive play.
op.colle-zukertort.name: Colle-Zukertort System
op.colle-zukertort.desc: A system with a fianchetto of the queen's bishop. Bb2 controls the diagonal and prepares the e3-e4 break with harmonious development.
op.india-dama-petrosian.name: Queen's Indian Petrosian
op.india-dama-petrosian.desc: a3 prevents ...Bb4 and prepares a solid center. White looks for d4+e4 with harmonious development and control of the center.
op.gda-deep.name: QGA Main Line
op.gda-deep.desc: Black returns the pawn to equalize in the center. A symmetrical piece-play position where accuracy is key.
op.holandesa-leningrado.name: Leningrad Dutch
op.holandesa-leningrado.desc: A double fianchetto with a pawn on f5. Black controls e4 and looks for a kingside attack with ...e5 and ...f4.
op.holandesa-muro.name: Dutch Stonewall
op.holandesa-muro.desc: Black builds a solid wall with pawns on d5-e6-f5. Control of e4 and a future kingside attack.
op.escocesa-clasica.name: Classical Scotch (Bc5)
op.escocesa-clasica.desc: Black develops the bishop actively aiming at d4. An open position with tactical play and pressure on the center.
op.india-rey-averbakh.name: King's Indian Averbakh
op.india-rey-averbakh.desc: The knight on e2 supports f4 and allows Bd2+Qd2 for queenside castling. An aggressive plan with play on the kingside.
op.nimzo-hubner.name: Nimzo-Indian Hübner
op.nimzo-hubner.desc: Immediate counterplay against d4. Black looks to pressure the center and eventually force ...Bxc3 at a favorable moment.
op.espanola-cambio.name: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation
op.espanola-cambio.desc: White simplifies but Black gets the bishop pair. Positional play with a structural edge for White.
op.espanola-breyer.name: Ruy Lopez: Breyer Variation
op.espanola-breyer.desc: The knight retreats to b8 to regroup on d7. A deep strategic maneuver that prepares a flexible counterattack.
op.espanola-marshall.name: Ruy Lopez: Marshall Gambit
op.espanola-marshall.desc: A pawn gambit that sacrifices material for an attack. Black gets active pieces, open files, and pressure on the king.
op.berlinesa.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence
op.berlinesa.desc: The Berlin Wall: an extremely solid queenless endgame. Black looks to equalize with the bishop pair and a flexible structure.
op.siciliana-acelerada.name: Accelerated Dragon
op.siciliana-acelerada.desc: A fianchetto without ...d6, avoiding the Yugoslav Attack. White can try the Maróczy Bind with c4.
op.siciliana-cerrada.name: Closed Sicilian
op.siciliana-cerrada.desc: A positional variation that avoids the Open Sicilian. Reciprocal fianchetto with quiet, strategic play.
op.siciliana-grand-prix.name: Grand Prix Attack
op.siciliana-grand-prix.desc: An aggressive attack with f4 looking to open the f-file and attack the king. Less theoretical than the Open Sicilian.
op.francesa-rubinstein.name: French Rubinstein
op.francesa-rubinstein.desc: Black exchanges on e4 and looks for solid play. The knight on e4 is active but Black gets a position free of weaknesses.
op.caro-kann-panov.name: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack
op.caro-kann-panov.desc: Transforms the Caro-Kann into a QGD-type position. Central tension with tactical chances for both sides.
op.escandinava-clasica.name: Classical Scandinavian Qa5
op.escandinava-clasica.desc: The queen on a5 keeps pressure on e1 and a2. Black looks for rapid development with ...Bf5 and ...e6.
op.ragozin.name: QGD: Ragozin Variation
op.ragozin.desc: Combines Nimzo-Indian ideas with the QGD. Bb4 pins the knight and creates dynamic pressure on the center.
op.nimzo-samisch.name: Nimzo-Indian Sämisch
op.nimzo-samisch.desc: White forces the exchange, getting the bishop pair and a strong center with doubled but active pawns.
op.nimzo-fischer.name: Nimzo-Indian Fischer
op.nimzo-fischer.desc: Fianchetto of the queen's bishop pressing e4 and the long diagonal. Flexible development with plans of ...Bb7 and ...c5.
op.india-rey-fianchetto.name: King's Indian: Fianchetto System
op.india-rey-fianchetto.desc: White fianchettoes both bishops. A positional setup where the long-term pressure of Bg2 is the key.
op.india-rey-petrosian.name: King's Indian: Petrosian Variation
op.india-rey-petrosian.desc: The knight retreats to support f3 and prepare g4. Deep positional control of the center and preparation of a kingside attack.
op.india-rey-bayoneta.name: King's Indian: Bayonet Attack
op.india-rey-bayoneta.desc: A queenside attack with b4-b5. White looks to open lines before Black launches the attack with f5.
op.benoni-cuatro-peones.name: Benoni: Four Pawns
op.benoni-cuatro-peones.desc: A massive center with four pawns. White has huge central presence but can be overextended.
op.benoni-fianchetto.name: Benoni: Fianchetto System
op.benoni-fianchetto.desc: A positional system where Bg2 pressures d5 and the diagonal. Black looks for counterplay with ...a6, ...b5, and on the e-file.
op.siciliana-smith-morra-deep.name: Smith-Morra Accepted
op.siciliana-smith-morra-deep.desc: After accepting the gambit, White gets rapid development, open files, and a strong initiative. Dangerous in rapid games.
op.falkbeer.name: Falkbeer Countergambit
op.falkbeer.desc: An aggressive countergambit that sacrifices a pawn for the initiative. Black gets a central advance and active play against the King's Gambit.
op.gambito-rey-rehusado.name: King's Gambit Declined
op.gambito-rey-rehusado.desc: Black declines the gambit and develops the bishop to c5 aiming at the weakened f2. A solid, active line.
op.panov.name: Caro-Kann: Deep Panov
op.panov.desc: A QGD-type structure with an Isolated Queen's Pawn. Dynamic play where both sides have clear plans: attack vs blockade.
op.escocesa-gambito.name: Scotch Gambit
op.escocesa-gambito.desc: A gambit that sacrifices d4 for development and control of f7. Similar to the Danish Gambit with open, tactical play.
op.holandesa-staunton.name: Staunton Gambit
op.holandesa-staunton.desc: An aggressive gambit that looks to open lines against the black king weakened by ...f5. Tactical play with compensation for the pawn.
